source_anchors.operation: n is clamped against MSExperiment::getSize(), which counts every spectrum's peaks plus every chromatogram point, while the vector that is sorted comes from get2DData and holds MS1 peaks only

std::partial_sort with that middle iterator is undefined when n exceeds tmp.size(), and the following loop indexes tmp[element_index] past the end; the sort is also not stable, so equally intense peaks may be cut arbitrarily
the PeakMap overload sets the column header size to n, the number of peaks actually written

the ConsensusMap-to-FeatureMap overload resizes the output and then assigns only the BaseFeature slice, so hulls, per-dimension qualities and subordinates stay default and the consensus handles and ratios are dropped
the FeatureMap overload takes the output's container unique ID from the input, which the source comment calls an arguable design decision
the FeatureMap overload sets the column header size to input_map.size(), the FULL input size, even when n truncated the copy
ConsensusFeature(UInt64, const Peak2D&, UInt64) builds the summary from the peak and inserts one handle identified by the element index
ConsensusFeature(UInt64, const BaseFeature&) uses BaseFeature(element, map_index), stamping map_index onto every copied peptide identification, then inserts FeatureHandle(map_index, element)
get2DData skips every spectrum whose MS level is not 1, which is why the conversion sees MS1 peaks only
getSize sums the peaks of all spectra AND all chromatograms, which is the count the clamp above uses
